what: ALIAS-SWEEP (2026-10-21): what the ExecutionPlanV1 alias law costs -- no two lifetimes of one bank live at once on overlapping bytes -- judged pairwise, as both rails judged it from S1-D to PX-3b-2, and by the sweep both rails judge it by now, against the steps a training pack carries: the C plan verifier with and without lent scratch, the lowering's one walk of the plan's and the pack's laws with and without it, the whole lowering beside the same lowering in the tree before ALIAS-SWEEP, and the Python codec's law both ways -- on the 9.84M comparison decoder's packs (vocabulary 260, width 384, 8 heads over 4 KV heads, 6 layers, FF 1024, tied; 8 sequences of 128 tokens; kblock+exp+reduce+attn, binary32, one thread) of 1, 2, 5, 10 and 20 steps; then the codec's law both ways over GEM's reuse shape at 2,000 to 32,000 lifetimes.
host: Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.10GHz, 4 vCPUs (PX-3b's AMX host); gcc (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0, the library at -O3 -ffp-contract=off -fno-math-errno; Python 3.11.15. sweep.json ran on a provisional commit of this change (2dcd37ad8aae) with an empty diff below bcir and runtime/c, and names the code by content: the git trees of bcir (e39da781f0c6) and runtime/c (42b3d4d5bb22), this commit's -- the records were added after the run, and no file below bcir or runtime/c changed. lower-before.json ran in a checkout of PX-3b-2's commit (8cc6b6be1c67: the tree before ALIAS-SWEEP, whose child, the aarch64 fix, changes one test, the history and the digest) with an empty diff, by that tree's own PX-2b driver (measurements/2026-10-20/px2b/lower.py) in an interpreter of its own: its code, not this tree's. Wall times are indicative: one virtualized host, one process at a time.

records.sweep.py: the driver: for each pack the step program stated as a pack and planned (native_pack.pack_artifacts), every verdict checked first -- the plan admitted by bcir_ep_verify, bcir_ep_verify_lent and the walk with and without scratch, and the codec's sweep naming the pairwise law's first alias -- then each row the median of REPS calls (the pairwise Python law of 3): ep_verify, ep_verify_lent, walk, walk_lent, lower_pack, py_pairwise, py_sweep; with --before CHECKOUT, that tree's own PX-2b driver run first, its lower_pack the lower_pack_before rows; last the codec's two laws over GEM's reuse shape (two spans of one bank, each value live two ticks), the sweep the median of 5 calls, the pairwise law one call and only to 8,000 lifetimes
records.sweep.json: sweep.py's run: each pack's claims, lifetimes, plan and pack bytes and the scratch its walk is lent, its rows, and the reuse shape's
records.lower-before.json: the parent tree's PX-2b lowering parts (lower.py) on the same packs, written by sweep.py --before
records.sweep.txt: the run's printed summary: the parent tree's rows first, then this tree's

reading: Both rails' alias law costs O(n log n) in the plan's lifetimes now, and every verdict is the pairwise law's. The whole lowering of a ten-step pack (2,231 claims, 1,686 lifetimes, a 207 KB plan) takes 26.8 ms against 51.2 ms in the tree before ALIAS-SWEEP (x1.91), a twenty-step pack's 51.2 against 149 (x2.91) and one step's 2.6 against 4.6 (binary32, one thread, the median of 15 calls). Its parts: the plan verifier 1.5 ms lent against 20.7 pairwise at ten steps (x13.9) and 2.8 against 70.4 at twenty (x25.2); the lowering's one walk of the plan's and the pack's laws 4.8 against 22.4 ms at ten (x4.66) and 9.5 against 78.7 at twenty (x8.29) -- what is left of the walk the records' own laws and the pack's claim checks. A walk is lent 62 bytes a lifetime and 4: 104,536 bytes for the ten-step plan, 195,056 for the twenty-step one's 3,146 lifetimes; the lowering lends the bytes of the executor it runs GEM's dispatch in afterwards, so its work buffer grows only where the sweep needs more. The Python codec's law: 6.2 ms against 82.2 at ten steps (x13.3) and 12.6 against 312 at twenty (x24.9); over GEM's reuse shape 5.1 ms against 148 at 2,000 lifetimes, 24.2 against 2,712 at 8,000 and 111 at 32,000, where the pairwise law was not run (about 43 s by its square). Every plan was admitted before it was timed, by both laws on both rails. In the tree before, the lowering's walk of the plan's and the pack's laws (bcir_ep_check_pack) took 36.5 of the ten-step lowering's 51.2 ms (71%, lower-before.json); the pairwise rows here are that law, unlent, in this tree.
witnesses: bcir/tests/test_execution_plan.py: the codec's sweep names the pairwise law's first alias on 3,000 crowded draws (equal ticks, touching spans, three banks) and on each draw moved apart, validate_plan's message the pairwise law's, the boundaries pinned; its cost n log n (16x the lifetimes under 64x the time); the C twin's verdicts -- bcir_ep_verify, bcir_ep_verify_lent on exactly bcir_ep_sweep_bytes of scratch at an odd address and on one byte less, the walk with and without scratch -- the codec's on 400 crowded plans, a third with a lifetime breaking its own law, the lifetimes the walk hands over the same both ways and no byte past the lent scratch written; the C sweep n log n and the lent walk under a quarter of the pairwise one at 32,000 lifetimes. bcir/tests/test_native_measured.py: the lowering's check walk returns the same status and hands over the same steps and lifetimes with scratch and without, on every refusal of test_native_run_pack. runtime/c/fuzz_streampack.c under libFuzzer, ASan and UBSan aborts where the lent verdict, or the lifetimes the lent walk hands over, differ from the pairwise ones.
faults: tools/testing/faults/alias-sweep.json AP1-AP8 (the codec's sweep) and alias-sweep-c.json AC1-AC10 (the C twin's sweep, its scratch and the walk's hand-over), each injected and caught by its own witness; ep-walk.json's EW5 and EW6, re-anchored to the walk's new arguments, each keeping its defect.
